subject: Charge harmonization and context-length splits for committed billing
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha@novacorp.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify token charging for long-context workflows / committed discount ask

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the proposal you sent last week (we attached internally). Before we move to Procurement, two quick things we need clarified on the billing side so we can sign the committed token discount:

1) Long-context sessions: Our agents send a ~6k prompt (context) + generated output. If the runtime splits that into two model calls (prefix + continuation) how are tokens accounted? We want to avoid double-charging the prefix if it's reused across calls in the same logical conversation.

2) Rounding/minimums: The draft mentions rounding to a charging quantum but doesn’t specify the quantum for long streaming calls (per-request vs per-session). For our usage pattern (many short agent utterances with reused context) understanding the quantum matters for the economics.

3) Fallback models / routing: We expect occasional fallback to smaller, cheaper variants. Will fallbacks be billed differently from the primary model (and could that defeat the committed discount math)?

If you can confirm the counting approach and whether you’ll make a billing-side harmonization for the committed tier (i.e., bill at the committed model rate regardless of fallback), we can move this to Procurement. Attaching our internal workbook with sample sessions — hope that helps.

Can we also get a short example invoice line for a 1M-token monthly commit? That will make the Procurement ask straightforward.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Cole

Hi Samantha —

Really useful questions, thanks for laying them out. High level answer first, then specifics and a recommended concession for the pilot so Procurement can sign quickly.

High level: for committed deals we can apply a harmonized metering approach so the customer is billed at the committed model’s unit rate independent of transient fallback routing. That avoids surprises when the runtime routes to cheaper variants. However, the underlying token accounting still reflects actual tokens used (so we can reconcile accuracy), and we then apply the committed-rate mapping in billing.

Details:
- Long-context and split calls: Metering is per-request (each HTTP/gRPC call is observed), but we apply a prefix-reuse credit when the same context prefix is sent again within a defined window. For this deal we propose: prefix credit of up to 70% for identical prefix strings seen within a 1-hour window for the same session_id. In practice that means if you send the same 6k prompt twice in an hour and only the latter call generated additional tokens, the billed tokens for the later call will reflect the reduced charge (tokens_charged = tokens_used - prefix_credit).

- Rounding / quantum: Our default rounding quantum is 100 tokens per-request. For committed monthly usage we can waive the per-request minimum and instead apply rounding at invoice line aggregation (monthly bucket rounded to nearest 1k tokens). That avoids micro-billing noise for high-volume commits.

- Fallbacks / harmonization: As mentioned above, for DEAL-7931 we propose billing at the committed model rate regardless of runtime fallback. We will still publish an audit column that shows model_variant and raw tokens so you can reconcile usage.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll loop in Karthik on the exact prefix-credit rules and Jordan on the commercial language for the SOW.
2) If that looks good, I’ll issue a v2 pricing PDF that shows a sample invoice line for a 1M-token commit using harmonized metering and the monthly rounding policy.

Available for a quick call — are you free tomorrow 9:30–10:00 PT?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Neha — quick technical notes to make the prefix-credit behaviour unambiguous for the SOW. Paste below so you can copy into the proposal.

On Tue, Sep 7, 2026 at 11:03 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Long-context and split calls: Metering is per-request (each HTTP/gRPC call is observed), but we apply a prefix-reuse credit when the same context prefix is sent again within a defined window. For this deal we propose: prefix credit of up to 70% for identical prefix strings seen within a 1-hour window for the same session_id.

Clarifications / examples:
- Definition of identical prefix: exact byte-for-byte match after normalization (normalize = collapse whitespace, standardize unicode NFKC). We do not attempt fuzzy prefix matching for billing credits.
- Session binding: credits apply when the request includes the same session_id header or when requests are within the same active conversation token window (we can define this as the same conversation_id for NovaCorp).
- KV-cache persistence: if the runtime serves the second call from a warmed KV cache (no re-encoding of the prefix), we still report raw_tokens for transparency and then apply the prefix_credit formula in billing.
- Rounding: the 100-token quantum is per-request for non-committed accounts. For committed accounts we will aggregate at invoice time and round the monthly subtotal to the nearest 1,000 tokens. Example: 1,001,420 raw tokens -> invoice rounds to 1,001,000 tokens for billing.

Edge case: cross-model routing where the prefix is sent to model_A and the continuation to model_B (rare). We will treat prefix_credit conservatively: prefix credited only if the continuation model is architecture-compatible for the same cached prefix (we'll include a small mapping table in the SOW). If that sounds complicated to legal, we can instead guarantee harmonized billing and avoid the per-call architectural check — that’s the simpler commercial route.

Happy to walk through a couple of sample rows from NovaCorp’s workbook to validate the numbers.

— Karthik

Samantha —

Thanks for the patience. Based on Karthik’s notes above, summary and the commercial concession we can offer for the pilot:

- Harmonized billing: NovaCorp will be billed at the DEAL-7931 committed model rate for all routed calls covered by the commit. We will include an audit column on the invoice that shows per-call model_variant and raw_tokens consumed.
- Prefix-credit: identical normalized prefixes will receive up to 70% credit when reused within a 1-hour window for the same conversation_id. We will include a worked example in the v2 PDF.
- Rounding: invoice-level aggregation will be rounded to nearest 1,000 tokens for committed monthly usage. No per-request minimum will be applied for committed buckets.
- Reconciliation: we’ll run a one-time post-launch reconciliation for the first invoice month and apply a catch-up or credit for any overbilling identified (one-time courtesy credit).

I’ve attached nova-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf (includes an invoice-line example for 1M commit) and a spreadsheet showing sample sessions mapped to billed tokens. If that matches your expectations, Procurement and your Legal team can sign the SOW and we’ll add the specific prefix compatibility table as an appendix.

Proposed times for a short wrap-up: Thu 09/09 9:30–10:00 PT or 11:00–11:30 PT. Tell me what works and I’ll send calendar invites.

Best,
